At Shifted Designs, we strive to shift the way we think, operate, and design. We're a growing civil engineering consultancy focused on delivering practical, innovative and sustainable solutions across a diverse range of projects.

- Liaise closely with engineers and project managers to deliver practical and cost-effective design solutions.

We’re looking for a Civil Designer (Civil 3D or 12D) to join our national team based in Melbourne.
Engineering for People, Place, Legacy.
Since 1958, TTW has been solving complex engineering problems for the people and places they serve. We're Australian owned, and we've grown by staying true to the quality work, honest relationships, and a genuine commitment to our clients and communities.
Our strength is our people. We support talented engineers to do their best work, and we invest in helping them grow. That's how we've earned our reputation for smart, sustainable engineering solutions across the sectors we know best.
Our Opportunity
We’re looking for a Civil Designer (Civil 3D or 12D) to join our national team based in Melbourne. In this role you will work across diverse, project-based assignments as part of a collaborative national team. The position of Civil Engineering Designer performs civil engineering technical tasks ranging from medium to high complexity. Designers will work independently or be responsible for leading a team of designers and CAD draftspersons to deliver quality detailed engineering models and drawings, in an efficient manner. The Civil Designer will also work within project design parameters, approved by the project director and\or project design manager.
Additionally, in this role you will
 - Assist project teams in Civil Engineering design, project management and in defining design parameters 
 - Development of civil engineering models in accordance with defined design parameters. 
 - Manage and mentor other civil engineering designers throughout project life cycles.
 - Resolve complex civil engineering design problems.
 - Undertake design checks in accordance with design parameters.   
 - Communicate all design components effectively and accurately with project teams.
Who we are looking for
 - Bachelor of Engineering or Technical College qualification (Advance Diploma Civil Engineering or approved equivalent)
 - Demonstrated experience (at least 5-7+ years) in a similar role
 - Comprehensive understanding of Civil Engineering, including a strong knowledge of Roads, Stormwater Drainage and Earthworks Design. 
 - Competency in Autodesk Civil 3D software.
 - Ability to develop Civil 3D Surfaces, Pipes and Earthworks Models to TTW national standardised frameworks. 
 - Ability to coordinate in ground infrastructure in accordance with relevant authorities.
 - Ability to read and implement local state standards. 
What will make you stand out
 - Highly developed communication skills to effectively communicate and coordinate with project team, clients, stakeholders, authorities, consultants, and contractors. 
 - A team player that works seamlessly with all levels of staff.
 - Highly developed written and verbal communication skills.
 - Problem solving/analytical skills with a great attention to detail.
Why Join TTW?
Our people are what make TTW who we are. We focus on giving you an environment where you can thrive both professionally and personally.
Here's what that looks like:
 - Flexible working arrangements
 - A strong focus on work-life balance
 - Health and wellbeing initiatives
 - Ongoing learning and professional development opportunities
 - Career progression within a collaborative global team
 - Exposure to diverse and challenging engineering projects
TTW is committed to fostering a work environment that is inclusive, supports flexibility, and welcomes diversity. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer.

The Civil Designer prepares concept and detailed designs, drawings, quantity schedules, cost estimates, and supporting technical documentation for the City’s capital works and infrastructure programs. candidates.content_text:
Summary 🔎
Feeling a bit bored where you are? Same types of projects, not much to get excited about?
Picture walking through the Melbourne CBD, looking up at a tower and thinking "I drew that." That's what this role offers.
You'll join a CBD-based structural team known for quality and technical depth. They have a strong high-rise pipeline, including a newly awarded 36 level mixed use development. If you've got solid concrete experience and want a new challenge where you can learn from some of the best in the industry, this one's worth a look.
Why this role stands out 📈
- A proper new challenge, with high-rise projects including a 36 level mixed use tower that's just been awarded.
- You'll work alongside and learn from some of the industry's leading engineers and senior drafters.
- Work that changes the Melbourne skyline, in a CBD office with strong project flow and a clear path to progress.
What you'll be doing 🧩
- Producing structural documentation in Revit for high-rise, mixed use and residential buildings.
- Modelling and detailing reinforced concrete and post-tensioned structures, including slabs, transfer structures, cores, columns and footings.
- Preparing GA plans, sections, details and reinforcement drawings.
- Coordinating with engineers, architects and services consultants in a BIM-led environment.
- Running clash detection and model coordination as the design develops.
- Supporting projects from concept through to construction documentation.
What we're looking for ✅
- Mid-level experience as a Structural Drafter in a consultancy or similar setting.
- Strong concrete experience, ideally on multi-storey or high-rise buildings.
- Advanced Revit Structure skills. AutoCAD is a bonus.
- Good working knowledge of Australian Standards and drafting conventions.
- Post-tensioned slab and reinforcement detailing experience is highly regarded.
- A careful eye for detail, and you're keen to keep learning.
- Australian working rights.
Software 💻
- Revit Structure (essential)
- AutoCAD (advantageous)
- Navisworks or similar coordination tools (a plus)
How to apply 📩
If you're ready for a new challenge and want projects you can point to in the Melbourne skyline, click Apply with your CV. You can also get in touch for a confidential chat.

bullets: 2:1 FIFO/BIBO roster during site execution.
Initial start in Brisbane office
Major gas turbine project in QLD
candidates.content_text:
Monadelphous is seeking a motivated and technically capable Civil Project Engineer to support the delivery of a major gas turbine power station project in Queensland.
This is a hands-on project delivery role with responsibility for coordinating civil construction work packages from engineering and procurement through construction, quality verification, commissioning support and close-out.
This role will suit an experienced Civil engineer who can provide technical leadership across civil and structural scopes while ensuring engineering compliance, construction readiness and successful project outcomes throughout the project lifecycle.
Working with Monadelphous offers many benefits, some of which include:
Competitive remuneration package, including applicable site uplift and project completion benefits:
- 2:1 FIFO/BIBO roster during site execution.
- Opportunity to deliver critical civil infrastructure on a major Queensland power project.
- Exposure to complex multidisciplinary interfaces across civil, structural, mechanical, electrical and commissioning works.
- Collaborative project environment with safety, quality and delivery accountability at its core.
Key Responsibilities will include:
- Lead the day-to-day delivery of assigned civil work packages, including: 
- Detailed earthworks, excavation, backfill and compaction.
- Reinforced-concrete foundations, slabs, bunds and equipment plinths.
- Roads, pavements, hardstands and car parks.
- Stormwater drainage, pits, culverts, swales and erosion controls.
- Underground services, trenches and service crossings.
- Buildings, structural works and multidisciplinary civil interfaces. 
- Review civil drawings, specifications, geotechnical information, survey data and design reports to confirm constructability and construction readiness. 
- Manage work packs, construction methodologies, material requirements and subcontractor scopes. 
- Coordinate civil interfaces with mechanical, electrical, structural, commissioning and external works contractors. 
- Provide field-engineering support to supervisors and subcontractors and promptly resolve technical and constructability issues. 
- Manage technical queries, RFIs, design changes, redline mark-ups, NCRs and as-built information. 
- Coordinate survey control, set-out verification, quantity surveys and completed-work records. 
- Prepare and maintain short-term look-ahead plans, progress updates, productivity reporting and labour, plant and material forecasts. 
- Monitor subcontractor performance, progress claims, variations, cost forecasts and package budgets. 
- Manage civil ITPs and quality records, including: 
- Earthworks compaction and geotechnical testing.
- Concrete sampling, slump and strength testing.
- Reinforcement and pre-pour inspections.
- Survey verification and as-built records.
- Material traceability, hold points and completion dossiers.
- Promote a strong culture of safety, collaboration, accountability and continuous improvement.
What you'll bring:
- Degree qualification in Civil or Structural Engineering. 
- Proven construction experience delivering civil scopes. 
- Current RPEQ registration, or eligibility and willingness to obtain RPEQ. 
- Experience on gas-fired power generation, power-station, Balance of Plant or EPC construction projects. 
- Experience delivering civil works around major electrical or mechanical equipment.
- Demonstrated success in a Project Engineer, Civil Engineer or similar project delivery role. 
- Strong understanding of multidisciplinary engineering and construction delivery within major project environments. 
- Sound knowledge of Australian Standards, engineering governance and design compliance requirements. 
- Practical knowledge of civil QA/QC requirements
- Ability to provide engineering assurance and make informed technical decisions in a construction environment. 
- Strong commercial acumen, including exposure to project costs, procurement activities and contract variations. 
- Experience with planning, progress measurement, cost forecasting, variations and progress claims.
- Excellent stakeholder engagement and coordination skills across clients, contractors, consultants and project teams. 
-  A demonstrated commitment to safety, quality and delivering projects to schedule.
- Ability to communicate clearly and make timely, practical engineering decisions in a site environment.
Life at Monadelphous
There’s lots to get involved in, celebratory or cultural events and so much more. We work hard to make Monadelphous a truly great place to work.
We celebrate our diversity and shared values and are committed to inclusion and equal opportunities for all. We’re committed to hiring locally, encourage people of all diverse backgrounds to apply and strongly encourage women and First Nations people to submit an application.
About us
Monadelphous is an ASX-200 company providing multidisciplinary construction, maintenance and industrial services to many of the largest companies in the resources, energy and infrastructure sectors. Established in 1972, we’ve been working in Australia and around the world for more than 50 years. We work on the biggest projects and ensure our teams have a variety of opportunities available to follow their career path of choice.
Our Engineering Construction division is an increasingly diverse business, focusing on managing and delivering large-scale project management and construction services. Our expertise includes civil construction, structural steel fabrication, modularisation and delivery, as well as structural, mechanical, piping and tank construction. We also specialise in heavy lift and haulage services, electrical and instrumentation work and renewable energy infrastructure.
Safety is at the forefront of everything we do, and we live by our promise: The Safe Way is the Only Way. Apply now to get started. A career at Monadelphous is a career with a difference. Make it yours.

candidates.content_text:
You’re an experienced civil engineer looking to take the next step in your career. You will be working on civil projects across built form, road infrastructure, high-density precinct development, and public domain works.
 This role is based at our Sydney office.
 What You’ll Own
 As a Civil Engineer - Construction, you will join a professional and collaborative team of engineers, designers, drafters, graduates and undergraduates working across a diverse portfolio of civil and infrastructure projects.
 You will work closely with contractors, clients, project managers and design engineers throughout the construction phase and be responsible for activities including:
 - Undertaking civil construction inspections and preparing associated inspection records and reports.
 - Reviewing and administering Hold Points and Witness Points.
 - Reviewing contractor Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs) and associated construction quality documentation.
 - Reviewing material submissions, product approvals, shop drawings and technical documentation for compliance with the design intent and project requirements.
 - Responding to RFIs and assisting with the resolution of construction and site-based technical issues.
 - Reviewing non-conformances, defects and proposed construction departures in consultation with the design team.
 - Supporting construction verification, certification and project close-out activities.
 - Coordinating with contractors, clients, authorities and multidisciplinary design teams.
 - Maintaining clear records of inspections, decisions, approvals and outstanding construction actions.
 - Supporting the administration and delivery of TfNSW Independent Project Verification (IPV) projects.
 - Assisting with technical reviews, verification activities, registers, submissions and close-out requirements associated with TfNSW projects.
 - Providing practical engineering input that considers both design intent and construction methodology.
 The role will provide exposure to projects across transport infrastructure, industrial, built environment, public domain and land development sectors.
 While the position is primarily construction focused, there will also be opportunities to contribute to design reviews and civil design activities where appropriate.
 Why Northrop
 We’re employee owned. That means the people working in our business have a genuine stake in its future.
 There are no external shareholders or overseas parent company. Decisions are made by people who understand our work, our clients and our people. Our leaders are accessible, and when you have an idea for doing something better, you’ll be encouraged to share it.
 For more than 50 years, we’ve built our business around our people, our relationships and the impact our work has on communities.
 Today, our multidisciplinary teams work across NSW, ACT, Queensland and Victoria on projects of all sizes, spanning sectors including health, education, residential, commercial, industrial, sport and land development.
 What You Bring
 - 5+ years of relevant civil engineering experience, with demonstrated exposure to the construction phase of civil or infrastructure projects.
 - Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering from a recognised university or institute.
 - Experience undertaking civil construction inspections and working with contractors on active construction sites.
 - Experience with Hold Points, Witness Points, ITPs, material approvals, RFIs and construction quality documentation.
 - A practical understanding of construction methodologies and the ability to assess whether completed works align with drawings, specifications and design intent.
 - Strong communication skills and confidence dealing directly with contractors, clients and project stakeholders.
 - The ability to manage multiple projects, inspections and competing priorities while working autonomously.
 - Strong written skills and the ability to maintain clear and defensible construction records.
 - TfNSW project experience is highly regarded, particularly experience with TfNSW construction, verification, surveillance, assurance or Independent Project Verification processes.
 - Previous civil design experience is preferred and will be valuable when reviewing construction issues, design changes and departures.
 - Experience across roads, drainage, earthworks, pavements, utilities and associated civil infrastructure will be well regarded.
 What’s In It For You
 - Industry-benchmarked salary with annual reviews, we pay properly and revisit it every year.
 - Paid parental leave for primary carers, maternity, and partners
 - Salary income protection insurance
 - Monthly one-on-one career development conversations, mentoring programs, and investment in both internal and external training
 - Free EAP and wellbeing support.  
 - A positive and enjoyable workplace with a supportive team, a relaxed culture, and regular opportunities to connect through social activities and company events throughout the year.
 - A diverse range of projects and opportunities, from small residential developments to major hospitals, and everything in between. With such a broad variety of work, there's always something new to keep your role interesting and rewarding.
 Ready?
 To apply for this role, please submit a comprehensive resume as well as a brief covering letter by clicking on the “Apply” tab.
 If this role is not quite what you are after but are interested in finding out more about future opportunities with Northrop, please head over to our EOI link:
 https://v2.forms.jobadder.com/f/WzDLJEnGePglWrqXoxNZ7A32Y
 Northrop is an equal opportunity employer. We actively welcome applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people of all genders, people with disabilities, neurodivergent people, and people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds. If you need any adjustments to participate in our recruitment process, let us know — we’ll make it work.

candidates.content_text:
Are you an experienced Civil Engineer ready for the next step in your career? With a strong pipeline of project work, we’re looking for a motivated engineer to join our Victorian Buildings Team in Melbourne.
You’ll be part of a well-established and growing team of engineers, delivering impactful projects across sectors such as data centres, health, education, sports and leisure, defence, aged care, retail, and commercial residential buildings.
At Stantec, we offer a collaborative culture, flexible work arrangements and a supportive environment focused on your growth. You’ll have access to tailored training, development programs, and long-term career opportunities within a global business.
Day to day tasks would involve
- Perform civil engineering design for building projects across various sectors, including preparing drawings, calculations, reports, and design criteria using CAD and civil design software.
- Prepare and review engineering documentation, ensuring accuracy and compliance with project standards throughout all phases.
- Collaborate with architects, structural engineers, and other disciplines to deliver integrated design solutions and attend coordination meetings.
- Assist with proposals, cost estimates, and project documentation, while supporting scope, budget, and scheduling discussions.
- Support construction phase activities, including reviewing shop drawings, responding to RFIs, and preparing site observation reports
- Deliver work aligned with professional standards, Stantec’s quality procedures, and contribute positively to team culture and continuous improvement.
To be successful for this role you'll need
- A Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering
- Ideally have 1–4 years of experience in civil design for building projects within an engineering consultancy environment. Projects within the Education, Health and Defence sectors would be advantageous however not compulsory
- Experience in drainage design as well as general civil including roads, earthworks and pavements is highly regarded
- Skills in design software such as Civil 3D, DRAINS, Music and AutoCAD is highly regarded
- Sound knowledge of relevant Australian Standards
- Strong knowledge of site development, stormwater management, and civil systems integration for buildings.
- Excellent communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively across disciplines.
- A proactive mindset with strong problem-solving and organizational skills.
What we offer
Along with a competitive salary we offer many other benefits to ensure your professional development & wellbeing is ongoing:
- Genuine Flexible Working Arrangements - Including work from home opportunities, provision for school term contracts, job sharing and part time employment.
- Option to purchase up to 4 weeks additional leave.
- Learning and Talent Development Programs - Including Global programmes, online learning and on-the-job learning
- Mentoring for your own development and the opportunity to mentor others
- A friendly team environment, with dedicated and enthusiastic staff committed to producing high quality service and deliverables
- Professional Memberships
- Salary Continuance Insurance (SCI)
- Mental Health and Wellbeing Programs
- Service Recognition Awards
- Employee Assistance Program
About Stantec
The Stantec community unites approximately 34,000 employees working in over 400 locations across six continents. We collaborate across disciplines and industries to bring buildings, energy, resources, water, environmental, transport and infrastructure projects to life.
Our work from initial project concept and planning through design, construction, and commissioning begins at the intersection of community, creativity, and client relationships.
Communities are fundamental. Whether around the corner or across the globe, they provide a foundation, a sense of place and of belonging. That's why at Stantec, we always design with community in mind.
We care about the communities we serve—because they're our communities too. We're designers, engineers, scientists, and project managers, innovating together at the intersection of community, creativity, and client relationships. Balancing these priorities results in projects that advance the quality of life in communities across the globe.
Culture
Stantec is serious about healthy work-life balance, diversity, inclusion & equity, indigenous relations, innovation, community engagement, corporate sustainability, and social wellbeing. We have employee groups for women, LGBTQI , neurodiversity, and more! Our employees play sport, fundraise, volunteer, learn, and have fun together.
We are committed to reconciliation and to building respectful relationships with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples. We’re better together when different perspectives are welcomed and valued, and we’re committed to a workplace where everyone can belong and thrive. If you need any adjustments to participate in our recruitment process, please let us know.
How to apply
If this position is of interest, please apply via the link below.
Please note that no agency applications will be accepted at this time.
